counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span explicitly states the words 'situs inversus totalis'
No abdominal imaging directly confirms complete abdominal situs inversus
decisive_items: apex of the heart located at the right side of the chest accompanied by hepatic dullness that was located in the left subcostal region
right atrium and right ventricle laid on the left side and the left atrium and left ventricle on the right side with its apex directed to the right
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete raw-span diagnosis: it combines right-sided cardiac apex, reversed atrial/ventricular anatomy on echocardiography, and left subcostal hepatic dullness, which together indicate dextrocardia with situs inversus totalis. R2 captures the cardiac reversal but omits the hepatic dullness span and the totalis qualifier. R1 only identifies the RBBB ECG pattern, which is a secondary finding after electrode relocation and does not address the underlying dextrocardia/situs inversus.

rejected.why: R1 labels only the complete RBBB ECG finding and ignores the decisive right-sided cardiac apex, reversed cardiac chambers, and left-sided hepatic dullness; it is therefore an incomplete and less likely diagnosis.
